findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so logs sent through it are never recorded
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a new, unrelated instance. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs only via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. As a result, the "Plugin Request Completed" entry never shows up in the injected TestLogger's `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs`. Any test that checks that this middleware logs, or checks the status/error params it logs, will see zero calls. The fake should return itself, or a logger sharing the same `Logs` storage, so that context-derived logs stay observable in tests.

findings.title: Moving pluginId/endpoint/dsUID/uname into context-only logging is untested and relies on middleware order
findings.body: `LoggerMiddleware` no longer logs `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` or `traceID` explicitly. These fields now appear on the `grafana-data-egress` log line only if `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` ran earlier in the chain and stored them via `log.WithContextualAttributes`. The PR adds no tests for the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, and none checking that the final log line still has these fields. If the middleware is reordered, omitted by another caller of `NewLoggerMiddleware`, or `FromContext` stops picking up the attributes, the egress log silently loses the plugin and datasource identifiers. A test that runs the real chain and asserts the logged key/values would catch such a regression.
